_doc: Curated technique seeds (knowledge_architecture.md section 5), one file per area. Fields: id, level + scope (a scope node or universal), aliases (v1 / technique-DB / footer names folded in), mechanism, preconditions (predicate DSL), predicts (canonical metric -> up|down|flat|up_or_flat|down_or_flat), risks (pitfalls), states / op_classes / op_kinds gates (empty = any), slot (offered by the multi-slot agent), prior {mean, n}: a seed prior with a low pseudo-count that evidence overrides, realizations by scope (target:<key> | target:<backend>:sm_NN+ | target:<backend> | node:<id> | universal). Loaded by Ontology.seed(); scripts/seed_knowledge.py builds a knowledge.db from these files.

techniques.mechanism: consecutive lanes touch consecutive addresses, so every memory transaction carries only useful bytes
risks: a transposed mapping can break coalescing of the other operand

realizations.how: Make consecutive threads / work-items touch consecutive addresses: map the fastest-varying lane index to the contiguous (innermost) dimension; transpose through on-chip memory when the natural mapping is strided.
Keep the unit-stride dimension innermost so vector loads are vle (unit stride), not vlse (strided).
Lay operands out so each mvin row is a contiguous DRAM run (row stride = DIM elements); transpose on the host side of the DMA, not per element.

techniques.mechanism: wider loads and stores per instruction: fewer memory instructions and more bytes in flight per lane
risks: misaligned base pointers or sizes not divisible by the vector width
forgetting the scalar tail

realizations.how: Use float4/float2 (half2 / __half2 for fp16, __nv_bfloat162 for bf16) loads and stores where alignment and sizes allow (check (uintptr_t)p % 16 and n % 4); keep a scalar tail.
Use vload4/vstore4 (float4, half8) where alignment allows; keep a scalar tail.
Strip-mine with vsetvli at LMUL=m4/m8 and vle32/vse32 so each instruction moves VLEN*LMUL bits.

techniques.mechanism: block / grid shape matched to the machine: enough resident warps and full waves, no idle tail
risks: more threads per block can cut registers per thread and spill

realizations.how: Choose block size (128-256 threads usually) and grid shape for occupancy and to cover small problems; a grid of a few waves of the SM count with grid-stride loops; cudaOccupancyMaxPotentialBlockSize is a good start.

Work-group sizes of 64 or 128 (multiples of the 64-wide Adreno wave); 256+ only for light kernels -- register-heavy kernels report a lower CL_KERNEL_WORK_GROUP_SIZE; global size covering every SP several times.
One hart: no launch geometry; choose the loop order so the vectorised loop is long (>= 4 * VLMAX).

techniques.mechanism: several independent operations per thread so the scheduler can issue while earlier ones wait on memory or the pipeline
risks: register growth lowers occupancy
on naive kernels compute_util can fall while time drops (fewer wasted instructions)

realizations.how: Unroll inner loops (#pragma unroll with a compile-time trip count) and give each thread several independent elements / accumulators to hide latency.
Unroll 4-8x with independent vector accumulators; in-order cores have no OoO to hide the load-use bubble.

techniques.mechanism: declare inputs non-aliasing and read-only so loads can be reordered, batched and served from the read-only path

realizations.how: Mark inputs const __restrict__ and use __ldg for read-only data.
Mark inputs __global const * restrict; for read-heavy 2D data see image2d_texture_reads.

techniques.mechanism: stage a reused block in fast on-chip memory so each DRAM element is read once per tile instead of once per use
risks: register spills at large tiles
bank conflicts
shared memory caps occupancy
missing __syncthreads between load and use

realizations.how: Tile the operands through __shared__ memory (e.g. 32x32 or 64x64 tiles), __syncthreads() per k-step, so each element is read from DRAM once per tile.
__shared__ tiles filled with cp.async (cuda::memcpy_async / __pipeline_memcpy_async) in a 2-3 stage pipeline.
Tile through __local memory with barrier(CLK_LOCAL_MEM_FENCE) per k-step (on Adreno local memory is not much faster than L1: tile in registers first, see register_tiling_over_local_memory).
Block loops so each block's working set stays L1-resident (32 KiB L1D); strip-mine the inner loop at VLEN.
Tile I/J/K so A, B tiles fit the 256 KiB scratchpad and C fits the 64 KiB accumulator (see scratchpad_tiling).

techniques.mechanism: each thread computes a TMxTN block of outputs in registers, reusing every loaded operand TM or TN times
risks: spills when TMxTN is too large
lower occupancy

realizations.how: Each thread computes a small TMxTN block of outputs in registers (outer-product micro-kernel over the k loop), operands read from on-chip tiles.
Keep a 4x4 (or LMUL-wide) accumulator block in vector registers across the reduction (vfmacc.vf); write back once.

techniques.mechanism: load the next tile while computing the current one, overlapping memory latency with arithmetic
risks: twice the on-chip buffer
pays off only when a kernel is already tiled

realizations.how: Prefetch the next shared-memory tile into registers (or a second buffer) while computing the current one.
cp.async into a second shared buffer with cp.async.wait_group; compute on the other.
async_work_group_copy the next tile into a second __local buffer, wait_group_events before use.
Software-pipeline: issue loads for iteration k+1 before the FMAs of iteration k; __builtin_prefetch 64-128 elements ahead.
Overlap mvin of the next tile with the current compute (Gemmini's ROB overlaps DMA and the array when tiles are double-buffered in the scratchpad).

techniques.mechanism: treat the convolution as a GEMM (M=N*OH*OW, N=OC, K=IC*KH*KW) without materialising im2col, so GEMM blocking applies
risks: index math per k-step
not worth it for depthwise convs (K=KH*KW is tiny)

realizations.how: Treat the convolution as a GEMM (M=N*OH*OW, N=OC, K=IC*KH*KW) without materialising im2col; decode (n,oh,ow) and (ic,kh,kw) from the GEMM indices and tile it like a GEMM.
im2col into an L1-sized buffer, then the vectorised GEMM micro-kernel.
Use the im2col unit (tiled_conv_auto) instead of host-side im2col.

techniques.mechanism: split one serial accumulation chain into independent partial sums combined at the end: depth N -> log N
risks: floating-point reassociation changes rounding

realizations.how: vfredusum.vs / vfredmax.vs over K independent vector partial sums; one final reduction.
Block-level tree reduction in on-chip memory, one partial per thread first.

techniques.mechanism: fewer passes over memory and fewer kernels: compute statistics and output in one sweep
risks: numerically different single-pass statistics (use Welford)

realizations.how: Compute statistics and the normalised output in as few passes over memory (and as few kernels) as possible; keep the row in registers / on-chip memory between passes.
Fuse the passes into one loop nest so intermediates stay in vector registers.

techniques.mechanism: precompute strides and divisions; fewer integer divides and multiplies per element

realizations.how: Precompute strides / divisions outside the loop; iterate the inner index and carry the outer instead of div/mod per element; use 32-bit indices when sizes allow.

techniques.mechanism: split the reduction (K) dimension across blocks when the output is too small to fill the machine
risks: an extra reduction pass / atomics; atomics change rounding order

realizations.how: Split K across blocks (a third grid dimension); each writes a partial tile, then a second small kernel (or atomic adds) sums them.

techniques.mechanism: one launch covers many instances or iterations, so per-launch overhead is paid once

realizations.how: Persistent kernel or CUDA graph over the instances; merge back-to-back kernels.

techniques.mechanism: cheaper instructions for transcendentals and divisions (intrinsics, polynomial approximations)
risks: accuracy outside the 1e-3 relative tolerance (tanh/erf near 0, exp overflow)

realizations.how: Use __expf/__logf/__fdividef/rsqrtf intrinsics where the tolerance allows; avoid double-precision literals (1.0 -> 1.0f); erff over a hand-rolled GELU series.
native_exp / native_divide / half_ intrinsics where the tolerance allows.
Degree-4 minimax polynomial after range reduction instead of libm expf/tanhf; vectorise the polynomial.

techniques.mechanism: fewer live registers per thread so more warps are resident to hide latency
risks: less register reuse

realizations.how: __launch_bounds__(threads, minBlocks), narrower live ranges, recompute cheap values instead of keeping them; check -Xptxas -v for spills.
Smaller unroll / fewer private arrays until CL_KERNEL_WORK_GROUP_SIZE reaches the device maximum; private arrays live in slow memory on Adreno.

techniques.mechanism: uniform control flow across a warp (predication, sorting work, hoisting bounds checks) so no lanes idle

realizations.how: Hoist bounds checks out of inner loops (interior / edge split), use selects (fminf/fmaxf, ternaries) instead of divergent branches.
Replace branches with vector masks (vmerge / masked ops) in the vectorised loop.

techniques.mechanism: less total work: a different algorithm, avoiding redundant computation or data movement
risks: correctness

realizations.how: Remove redundant work: precompute shared sub-expressions, avoid recomputing reductions, exploit structure (separability, sparsity, identity elements) in the op.

techniques.mechanism: half the bytes per element (fp16 / bf16 storage) and twice the arithmetic rate on fp16 paths
risks: fp16 accumulation exceeds tolerance: accumulate in fp32
bf16 keeps 8 significant bits: rounding an intermediate to bf16 costs ~4e-3 relative; keep intermediates in fp32

realizations.how: half2 loads (__half22float2) and fp32 math, store with __floats2half2_rn; never accumulate in __half. bf16: __nv_bfloat162 loads (__bfloat1622float2), fp32 math, store with __floats2bfloat162_rn (sm_75 has no bf16 arithmetic; the conversions compile everywhere).
vload_half4 / half8 loads with float math (cl_khr_fp16); Adreno runs half at 2x the float rate, so half math is fine for elementwise ops within tolerance.
Zvfh: vle16 + vfwcvt to fp32, compute, vfncvt back; or vfwmacc for widening accumulation.

techniques.mechanism: order work so blocks that share operands run close in time and hit in L2 instead of DRAM

realizations.how: Swizzle the block index (grouped / raster order, e.g. groups of 8 block rows) so concurrently running blocks share A/B tiles in L2.

techniques.mechanism: fewer, fatter threads: amortise index math and reuse operands across several outputs per thread
risks: too few threads for small problems

realizations.how: Give each thread 2-8 outputs (along the contiguous dimension), reusing loaded inputs and index math across them.

techniques.mechanism: apply bias / scale / activation / residual to the accumulators in registers before the single store, instead of separate passes
risks: only inside one slot: fusing across slots is a graph-level change (ModelBlaster proposals)

realizations.how: When the slot's op includes its epilogue (fused ops), apply the bias / activation / scale in registers right after the K loop and store once.

techniques.mechanism: do all the per-element math of a fused elementwise chain in registers in one pass over memory

realizations.how: Read each input element once, apply the whole chain (as the reference does) in registers, write once; vectorise the loads.
One strip-mined loop applying the chain in vector registers.
